clue.text: Alienate corrupt sergeant

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled or perverted from its proper form, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked army sergeant is pushing away the soldiers who serve under him.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to make them hostile or distant, a close synonym of alienate.

clue.text: Proudly raise letter to gaffer

blocks.note: the spelt-out name of the letter M, also a printer's measure
a gaffer is a foreman or boss in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone sends a letter to their manager and holds it up with pride.
explanation.walkthrough: A design that stands 'proud' sticks out from the surface, which is what embossing does.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossing raises a pattern in relief so it stands proud of the surrounding surface.

clue.text: Check tip of electrode on top of sperm-producing glands

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the following word is kept
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: to check is to test
the first letter of electrode
the first letter of sperm

explanation.surface: A medical instruction: examine the electrode tip placed over the reproductive glands.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sperm does double duty, supplying its first letter and also belonging to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Testes are the male reproductive organs in which sperm cells are made.

clue.text: Sperm whales' innards may contain this novelist pierced by ice floating in sea and river

definitions.text: Sperm whales' innards may contain this

indicators.note: something pierced has other material driven through its middle, so the next words sit inside

blocks.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, British novelists
an iceberg, shortened to berg
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A sentence about whale biology that drifts into talk of a writer, sea ice and rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the waxy lump really does form in a sperm whale's gut. Kingsley and Martin Amis are the crossword's favourite novelists.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance formed in the intestines of sperm whales, prized in perfumery.

clue.text: Go to get bishop, English bloke and god confused by unintelligible jargon

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up and must be put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sent to fetch a bishop, an Englishman and a deity is baffled by meaningless jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: Only English, bloke and god are muddled; GO and B stay in place at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbledegook is meaningless or incomprehensible language, especially pompous official wording.

clue.text: Worship, hoping to drown such music?

indicators.note: to drown something is to submerge it, so the answer lies sunk within the neighbouring words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Churchgoers hope their hymns will cover up the noise of a certain kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such music' points back to the letters sitting in the clue's own words.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip hop is a genre of popular music built on rapping over beats, from US urban culture.

clue.text: Disinclined to act in liner tragedy

indicators.note: in tells you the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the letters span the two words

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to take part in a shipping disaster, perhaps a passenger or crew member.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert describes something sluggish or lacking any inclination to move or take action.

clue.text: Musicians' rare piano is covered by tiles

indicators.note: something covered has another thing wrapped round it, so the earlier letters go within

blocks.note: R is a dictionary abbreviation for rare
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
taken as written
tiles is old slang for hats

explanation.surface: A musical group's unusual piano is sheltered beneath a tiled roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiles' looks like roofing but is dated British slang for hats, the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpists are players of the harp, so they are a type of musician.

clue.text: Man pares freshly made cheese

indicators.note: something freshly made has been newly put together, so the letters form a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook trims slices off a wheel of newly produced cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese, often grated, so it is an example of the defined category.

clue.text: Primate hard at work catching hard black sailor

indicators.note: catching means seizing and holding, so the outer word grips the following letters

blocks.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
B is the abbreviation for black
AB, able-bodied seaman
someone hard at work is busy

explanation.surface: An ape toiling away grabs a tough, dark-skinned seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'hard' belongs to the phrase 'hard at work'; only the second gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby, or galago, is a small nocturnal African primate with big eyes.

clue.text: Animal claiming a right to be more treasured

indicators.note: claiming something means taking hold of it, so the animal surrounds what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: A creature asserting its entitlement to be loved more than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' is vague: it is the deer, which surrounds A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means beloved or cherished, so its comparative form means more cherished.

clue.text: Charge for chap's expression of amusement?

blocks.note: a chap is a man, with the possessive kept
laughter is how amusement is shown

explanation.surface: Asking what price a fellow's chuckle would fetch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' reads as a fee but is a criminal charge; the question mark flags the split reading of the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is a criminal offence a person can be charged with: unlawful killing without intent.

clue.text: That girl meeting the Queen is thin

blocks.note: the pronoun for that girl
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A slender young woman is introduced to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is very fine and see-through, so the word can mean thin.

clue.text: Not most knowledgeable, however

blocks.note: the opposite of most
wise means knowing much

explanation.surface: A grudging remark that someone is hardly the brightest, but still.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastwise is an informal adverb meaning at least or anyway, used like however to qualify a statement.

clue.text: Deal with worrying satanic plant

indicators.note: worrying at something means tugging it about, so these letters are pulled into a new order

blocks.note: to deal is to trade
taken as written

explanation.surface: Coping with a houseplant that seems devilishly troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradescantia, or spiderwort, is a genus of plants popular as trailing houseplants.

clue.text: Gobsmacked to get a point before rugby free-for-all

blocks.note: taken as written
a point of the compass
a ruck is a loose scrum in rugby, a general melee

explanation.surface: A rugby player is stunned at scoring just before a messy scramble for the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobsmacked is British slang for utterly astonished, the same state of amazement as awestruck.

clue.text: Sheath for poet following evidence of the pox?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the poet is placed after the sign of the pox, not before it

blocks.note: a scab forms over a pox sore
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A cover sought for a versifier who has been visibly marked by disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that holds a sword or dagger when not in use.

clue.text: Collapsed prostrate during action

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece is set in the middle of the other

blocks.note: lying prostrate is lying flat
a deed is an action

explanation.surface: Someone fell down and lay face down in the midst of the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deflated has had the air let out and sunk in on itself, as a punctured balloon does.

clue.text: Chief to tease Greer struggling with piece of kitchen equipment

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so these letters are thrown into a different order

blocks.note: CH is a short form of chief
taken as written
taken as written; Germaine Greer, the feminist writer

explanation.surface: A boss teasing Germaine Greer while she battles with a kitchen gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheese grater is a kitchen utensil with sharp-edged holes for shredding cheese.

clue.text: Hang about in ladies' underwear that is not visible

indicators.note: what is not visible has gone from sight, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: lingerie is women's underwear
i.e., Latin id est

explanation.surface: Someone loiters wearing underwear that cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation for 'that is' comes off the end of the underwear word.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay around longer than needed, which is what hanging about means.

clue.text: Fed up with death in shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
death is one's end

explanation.surface: A refugee sick of mortality takes cover in a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like the phrase meaning weary, but up is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelter someone is to protect them from harm, which is to defend them.

clue.text: Charge for a water pipe by branch of a river in Australia

definitions.text: branch of a river in Australia

blocks.note: a bill is a charge
taken as written
a bong is a water pipe for smoking

explanation.surface: A plumber's invoice for a pipe laid beside an outback stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A billabong is an Australian word for a backwater or oxbow left by a river's side channel.

clue.text: Make amends an hour after midnight

blocks.note: first meaning: put a wrong right
second meaning, read as two words: the time one o'clock in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone apologises in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into two words naming a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make reparation for a sin or wrong, and the split form names 1am.

clue.text: Journey to get last bit of ungulate's offal

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a trip is a journey
the final letter of the hoofed animal

explanation.surface: Travelling to obtain the innards of a hoofed animal, as a butcher might.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle or sheep eaten as food, a kind of offal.

clue.text: Novelist, say, taking gold for "God"

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Thor, the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A writer accepts payment in gold in exchange for a deity, as if trading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' reads as 'in exchange for' but simply places the gold before the god.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is one example of an author, a writer of books; 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: German government put in control after street fight

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so these letters are set within the next word

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
G is the abbreviation for German
G is the abbreviation for government
to rule is to control

explanation.surface: Berlin's administration takes power once a street brawl has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German government' reads as one idea, but each word supplies its own abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A struggle is a violent effort or contest, a fight between opposing sides.

clue.text: Bash against Director General and setter, reversing in small electric car

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word for the setter is read from its end

blocks.note: a bash or do is a party
the standard abbreviation
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A crash between the BBC's chief and the crossword compiler while backing up in a fairground car.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgem is a small electrically powered bumper car at a funfair, driven to collide with others.

clue.text: Skint and embarrassed, traded in goods for commission

blocks.note: skint is British slang for having no money
red in the face with embarrassment

explanation.surface: A penniless, red-faced dealer who has been reduced to selling on commission.
explanation.definitionFit: Brokered means acted as a broker, an agent who buys and sells for others in return for a fee.
